prerequisites: Previous knowledge about Internet protocols is preferable.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding of the architecture of an IoT system.
Acquire knowledge related to the fundamental elements of the Python programming language.
Knowing how to code simple programs in Python through the use of functions, arrays, tuples and dictionaries.
Understanding of the architecture of the ESP32 board, and its digital inputs/outputs.
Understanding of the principle of operation of simple sensors and actuators.
Acquisition of basic knowledge related to the MicroPython framework.
Knowing how to setup simple circuits with resistors, LEDs, buttons and sensors on breadboards.
Knowing how to write MicroPython programs for ESP32 to acquire data from sensors.
Knowing how to write MicroPython programs for ESP32 that allow to control DC and servo motors.
Knowing how to code a driver in MicroPython for a simple sensor provided with interfacing via serial protocol.
Understanding of the Publish&Subscribe paradigm and the fundamental characteristics of the MQTT protocol.
Knowing how to encode in MicroPython a program for ESP32 that allows data exchange via MQTT protocol.
Understand the concepts behind designing user interfaces for IoT solutions.
Understand how Node-RED develops flow-based.
Knowing how to develop and implement Node-RED flows for the creation of monitoring and remote control dashboards of IoT solutions.
Knowing how to integrate an MQTT based IoT solution into OpenHAB.
Understanding and knowing how to interpret a project specification for an IoT system.

Knowing how to develop and implement from a hardware / software point of view an IoT system, based on a specific date, consisting of one or more microcontrollers connected to a set of sensors and actuators.
Architecture of an IoT application.
Programming of a microcontroller and sensors interfacing.
Characteristics of the different types of sensor (MEMS, SERVO).
Network protocols.
Create simple IoT applications in which the data detected by one or more sensors are processed through a microcontroller.

syllabus_topics: INTERNET OF THINGS. General Introduction. Examples of applications. Architecture of an IoT application. IoT frameworks.
Python expressions and variables. Selection and iteration. Definition of functions.
Arrays, tuples and dictionaries. Python exercises and examples.
ESP32 board overview: architecture and key features. The MicroPython framework.
GPIO. Management of digital outputs and digital inputs; analog inputs via ADC. First examples of development in MicroPython.

Organization of a breadboard and setup of simple circuits with LEDs, resistors and potentiometers. Examples of GPIO management with MicroPython and ESP32: turning a LED on, reading a button level, reading signals from a photoresistor. Management of a potentiometer.
Introduction to Pulse Width Modulation (PWM). First examples PWM with ESP32: control of LED light intensity - fading.
PWM examples. Control of the timbre and intonation of a passive buzzer. Speed control of a DC motor. Rotation control of a servo motor.
Introduction to serial protocols: RS232, I2C, SPI. Example of an I2C driver for a light intensity sensor.
Development of an I2C driver for a temperature and humidity sensor.
The Publish&Subscribe paradigm and the MQTT protocol. Service Quality Levels in MQTT. Development of a Python MQTT client with Eclipse Paho. Types of loop functions and callback functions.
Connection of the ESP32 microcontroller to the WiFi network and communication via socket module. Use of the MicroPython MQTT library for ESP32 and development of a "smart" light intensity sensor.
More MQTT examples on ESP32. Example of a complete IoT project. Tools for the creation of simple graphical interfaces.
Overview of tools for creating remote dashboards for IoT solutions. Introduction to Node-RED.
Implementation of simple Node-RED flows for interaction with MQTT and HTTP services. The Dashboard package. Persistence of acquired data.
Web-based platforms for smart homes. Introduction to OpenHAB. Integration of an MQTT based solution in OpenHAB.
Presentation of projects and start of activities.
assessment_rules: The exam includes a group project and a theoretical test. The project should involve interfacing sensors via I2C or SPI, controlling a device via PWM, and communicating via MQTT. The theoretical test verifies understanding of MQTT, I2C, SPI protocols, and PWM for motor control. The final grade is a weighted average of the project score (60%) and the theoretical test score (40%). Students achieving maximum scores in both and completing a project with unpresented sensors will be awarded excellence.
